I have farmed these 3 mu in Quzhou for 25 years. I never went to school, but I know my land with my hands and my eyes. Last year my wheat gave me about 500 kg per mu and my maize about 550 kg. It was an okay year, not great, not bad. I do what I always do because change is dangerous.

For wheat, I sow in October with improved seeds I buy from the input shop in town. Before sowing, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu — that is 50 jin per mu, costs about 150 yuan a bag. Then in March or April when the wheat turns green and starts shooting up, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 25 jin per mu. My neighbor Aunt Li skipped the urea one year and her wheat turned yellow and thin, so I never skip it. I would rather waste some fertilizer than lose yield. I irrigate three times: once at sowing if the soil is dry, once when the wheat is jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Well water costs electricity, but 3 mu is small so I can manage the pumping cost. I spray twice — once for weeds before sowing, and once in spring for aphids and rust. I till with the rotary machine every year, never deep plough. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For maize, right after I cut the wheat in early June, I run the rotary tiller quick and plant the maize the same day or the next day. The window is tight, but I have done it for 25 years. I use hybrid seeds — everyone in the village does now, the yield is much better than the old kind. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, same as wheat. Then when the maize is about knee-high, at the big trumpet stage, I put another half bag of urea. I irrigate twice — once after planting if it is dry, and once when the tassels come out. If August is very hot and dry I might do a third time, but usually twice is enough and saves electricity. I spray twice, for weeds and for armyworms. I hope for 550 kg per mu.

My sons work in Shijiazhuang and send some money home, so I can buy the inputs. But I still count every yuan. Three mu means three bags of compound for wheat, three bags for maize, plus urea. That is over 1,000 yuan just for fertilizer. It is a lot of money for our family. Still, I would rather spend a little more than risk a bad harvest. A bad year means no money for my granddaughter's school fees and no money for medicine. So I copy what my neighbors do, and I do what I did last year. That is how I stay safe.
